# ostree

[ostreedev/ostree](https://github.com/ostreedev/ostree) · OSS-Fuzz: [projects/ostree](https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/bd2ce21991a94a362b92fb1bf25f86d5a1a60842/projects/ostree)

**Status: available.** 5 of OSS-Fuzz's 5 fuzz targets have statements. 20 binaries, 26 MB. 59 statements: 0 proved, 0 known false, 0 suspected false, 14 blocked by the model, 45 open.

Built from ostree (commit `1d5a312a`).

## At a glance
| harness | what it does | checks beyond "does not crash" | statements |
|---|---|---|---|
| [fuzz-bootconfig](fuzz-bootconfig/) | Writes the input to a temp bootloader-entry file (optionally using a '+'-prefixed input prefix as the tries-counter filename suffix), parses it with ostree_bootconfig_parser_parse_at, calls the tries/get getters, writes it back with ostree_bootconfig_parser_write_at and clones it; every result and error is discarded. The written-back file is never re-parsed or compared (a parse->write->parse roundtrip was available but not checked). | none | 13, 7 blocked by the model |
| [fuzz-bsdiff](fuzz-bsdiff/) | Runs bsdiff(old=input, new=fixed 536-byte ramp) into a GMemoryOutputStream; bspatch.h is included and a bspatch_stream declared but never used, so the patch is never applied back and compared (no diff->patch roundtrip). | none | 13 |
| [fuzz-content-stream](fuzz-content-stream/) | Parses the input (top bit of byte 0 selects compressed) as an ostree content-object stream with ostree_content_stream_parse(trusted=FALSE); the returned file_info/xattrs/content stream and the error are discarded. | none | 13 |
| [fuzz-repo](fuzz-repo/) | Creates an archive-mode repo in a temp dir, sets config key [input] input=input, writes, reloads the config and reads min-free-space-bytes; all return values and errors ignored. | none | 7, 7 blocked by the model |
| [fuzz-rfc2616-date](fuzz-rfc2616-date/) | Parses the input with _ostree_parse_rfc2616_date_time and calls the GDateTime year/month/day/hour/minute/second getters, discarding the values; nothing is compared (no format->parse roundtrip, no range check). | none | 13 |

## What the statements say, for ostree
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.
- **`<build>_disagrees_at_most b`**: for inputs drawn from the harness's `Distribution.v`, the plain and sanitizer builds disagree with probability at most *b*.
- **`<build>_agreement_decidable`**: some riscv64 program decides exactly the finite inputs on which the two builds agree. A program that does so, with a bound on how often it rejects, is a route to a disagreement bound (docs/statements.md).

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch ostree
    ./oft verify-sha ostree

By hand: download `ostree-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.10.0](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.10.0), unpack it into `projects/ostree/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; an OSS-Fuzz testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [ostreedev/ostree](https://github.com/ostreedev/ostree) at `1d5a312a3189b0fbd70fe6769aadb19a366fedb2`, built with autotools
- Harnesses: unmodified
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. A binary whose SHA-256 differs after a rebuild with it is a bug: please open an issue.

## Licence
The licence of ostree is not recorded here yet. Each binary is a combined work of ostree, the harness, the C library, the compiler's runtime and every library it links; the SPDX expression of each is not recorded here yet. Corresponding source, in release [v2026.10.0-src](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.10.0-src): `ostree-src.tar.zst`, the upstream source trees exactly as upstream publishes them; `ostree-src.MANIFEST.tsv`, which says where the build lays each one down; and `recipe.tar.zst`, that release's build recipe (the build scripts, pins and patches). Its binaries are under a GPL-family licence, so their corresponding source also takes `toolchain-src.tar.zst`, the source of the toolchain they were built with, and `sysroot-src.tar.zst`, the source of every library they link from the build image, in release [sources-v1](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/sources-v1).
